attributes.location: South-east Cameroon, within the Congo Basin rainforest.
attributes.history: A hunting reserve in 1950, a wildlife reserve in 1973 and a Biosphere Reserve in 1981.
attributes.people: The Baka are allowed to hunt by traditional methods, while farming and professional hunting are banned.

content.name: Diy-Gid-Biy Cultural Landscape of the Mandara Mountains

attributes.type: Cultural World Heritage Site, the first for Cameroon.
attributes.inscribed: 11 July 2025, at the 47th session of the World Heritage Committee in Paris.
attributes.location: Far North Region, in the Mayo-Tsanaga Department, on the border with Nigeria.
attributes.description: Sixteen dry-stone archaeological sites, called Diy-Gid-Biy, in seven villages, with agricultural terraces and sites of worship, over about 2,500 hectares.
attributes.dates: The ruins date from the 12th to the 17th centuries.
attributes.criterion: Criterion (iii): a testimony to a vanished civilisation.
attributes.national_status: A national heritage site by Ministerial Order No. 0002/MINAC/SG of 28 February 2019.

content.name: Cameroon on the UNESCO World Heritage List

attributes.sites: Three: the Dja Faunal Reserve (1987), the Sangha Trinational (2012) and the Diy-Gid-Biy Cultural Landscape (2025).
attributes.ratified: Cameroon ratified the World Heritage Convention in 1982.
attributes.tentative_list: In 2020 Cameroon had submitted 20 sites to the tentative list: 12 cultural, 7 natural and one mixed.
attributes.intangible_heritage: The Nguon rites of the Bamoun people and the Ngondo of the Sawa are on the Intangible Cultural Heritage list.
attributes.caution: Check UNESCO for any inscription made after July 2025.
